title: Add 2026 Research Explorer with sourced catalog, scoped rankings and test queue
body:
## Why

Engineering Atlas needs a large, searchable research queue that connects current sources to fair comparisons and reproducible experiments. Popularity, publisher benchmarks, community experience and retained Atlas measurements need explicit scopes so discovery does not become an unsupported universal leaderboard.

## What changes

- Add a dependency-free GitHub Pages Research Explorer with search, 18 fields, type/maturity/evidence/year/track filters, shareable views, four-entry comparison, CSV export and proposed-test-plan export.
- Add 154 sourced entries, including 19 papers and 81 evaluation tracks; 166 catalog primary sources and 123 dated GitHub repository snapshots.
- Keep editorial priority, stars, reviewed community reports, publisher benchmark cohorts and Atlas measurement cohorts separate. Missing data stays missing; each measurement retains metric, direction, protocol and limitations.
- Import 27 existing JSON observations in nine cohorts from immutable retained evidence, and eight publisher-reported configurations in two external cohorts. No new candidate benchmark or production acceptance is claimed.
- Add 16 concrete proposed experiments, a dated research review, full generated catalog, methodology and community moderation guide.
- Add a public rating form, fail-closed approval ingestion, stable-account deduplication, error-preserving snapshots and a manual read-only refresh workflow producing a reviewable artifact. The initial approved rating count is zero.
- Prepare four complete wiki pages and append-only navigation blocks in `docs/wiki-research/`. Publishing the separate wiki still requires its authenticated interface.
- Preserve the latest upstream Site Adapters contribution. No adapter page, adapter catalog or collection-engine file is changed.

## Validation

- Uploaded Git tree matches the locally verified tree exactly.
- Python: 166 tests pass after integration with current main.
- JavaScript: 145 individual tests pass; the normal CI invocation also passes all 18 test files.
- Research structure: 525 registered sources, 131 Markdown files, no stale IDs.
- Research Explorer, card-lab and media-lab generated-asset checks pass.
- Browser: search, shortlist comparison, retained JSON ranking, publisher ProgramBench ranking, empty community ranking and narrow responsive layout inspected.
- Retained validation record: `experiments/research-explorer-validation/`.

## Known limits

- Browser automation reported failed CSV/JSON downloads and did not retain saved files. Export payload/scope/formula-safety tests pass; actual saved-file verification is still open in this environment.
- This is a dated curated snapshot, not exhaustive coverage or an assertion that the newest project is best.
- Publisher results are an imported subset and are not Atlas reproductions or equal-budget claims.
- The refresh workflow does not auto-commit or deploy; refreshed data is reviewed before publication.

## Concurrent-update integration

Merged main commit `50aba7a` into this branch without overwriting its archive-buffer reuse changes or retained evidence. The two append-only source-register conflicts are resolved by preserving every upstream entry and both documentation additions. Re-ran 166 Python tests, all 18 JavaScript test files, research structure and generated Explorer checks on the integrated tree. Protected adapter and application paths have no diff against the new main.
author: Herbertofury

title: Consolidate 2026 stack research into 20 searchable decision layers
body:
The catalog needs a practical path from broad discovery to decisions across application, game and modding stacks. This change consolidates that path into the existing Explorer, guides and wiki copies.

## What changes

- Add 61 candidates and update 22 existing records: 215 candidates, 22 papers, 355 distinct primary URLs, and 173 dated public repository observations.
- Add 20 stack layers with reference choices, alternatives to compare, research watchlists and adoption gates. Generate the existing stack-selection map from the same data.
- Extend search, shared URLs, CSV and test-plan exports with stack layers. Keep editorial roles separate from popularity, community reports and exact benchmark cohorts.
- Expand the existing test queue to 20 planned comparisons, including mod resolution, verified installation/rollback, extension lifecycle and asset fidelity.
- Preserve all 525 prior source records, all 123 earlier repository observations and historical measurements. Add 201 dated source observations, including release/channel conflicts and unavailable-artifact limits.
- Update the existing research documentation and three existing wiki publication copies. No new topical guide/wiki pages; Site Adapters and its implementation remain untouched.

## Validation and review

- 176 Python tests and 151 JavaScript cases pass; the standard Node command passes all 19 test files.
- Deterministic build, 726-record source/structure validation and whitespace checks pass.
- Browser checks cover layer filtering, scoped candidate links, dated-star ordering, reset, mod ecosystem constraints and a narrow 375-pixel content viewport without horizontal overflow.
- Review repaired stale legacy layer maps, malformed layer rows, misleading role assignments and duplicate-URL headline counting. Validation history and output logs are retained.
- Current upstream event-log recovery work is preserved; the latest wiki Experiment Evidence change was read before preparing publication.

## Evidence limits

This is research and implementation validation, with zero new candidate benchmark results or target acceptance. Existing 27 Atlas observations and eight publisher observations remain separate. The community snapshot still has zero approved reports. Browser saved-download verification remains limited by the previously recorded provider failure; payload and export-scope contracts pass. Updated wiki copies will be published and byte-verified separately after merge.

title: Expand site adapters to 349 scopes and add verified itch.io extraction
body:
## Why

The published adapter research was missing the executable extraction work, the second-round site evidence, and the requested itch.io and paid-platform coverage.

## Changes

- Expand the catalog to 349 service/scope entries with operation-specific evidence and explicit access limits.
- Add eight offline extraction families, sanitized actual-source replay receipts, and a dedicated itch.io parser with nine defensive tests and two real DOM replay cases.
- Cover post bodies, stable author IDs, separate author avatars, ordered media, release/file metadata, pagination, and local versus native following.
- Update all six game guides and add 414 primary-source records through the existing additive source register.
- Preserve current main research, CI checks, and unrelated wiki mappings. Keep GameSync Next unchanged until comparative acceptance.

## Validation

- All 50 files committed through the signed-in GitHub browser and read back in full against the prepared candidates; catalog raw-view bytes match SHA-256 587541035a801f554ad69db09c1b197a09f75807e44866d59c87f7c8b82c255b.
- Local current-main source/link validation: 1,778 sources, 157 Markdown files, zero stale sources.
- Current-main Python suite covered 242 tests; the one missing captured dependency was supplied and its targeted test passed. Explorer generated-file check passed.
- Normal repository CI remains enabled and must pass before merge.

## Scope limits

Research coverage is not universal working-adapter acceptance. Paid downloads, native follow actions, video playback, and unavailable login fixtures retain explicit pending states. Raw private captures and downloaded mods are excluded. Two historical screenshot binaries remain locally retained and are explicitly marked deferred in their receipt. Wiki publication status will be reconciled after the successful main merge.

title: Expand adapter communities to 426 scopes and add verified social extraction
body:
## Why

The adapter catalog needs concrete creator, post, media, release-file and follow methods across the communities where modders publish. A site name or readable preview alone does not establish complete extraction.

## Changes

- Expand the canonical catalog from 349 to 426 scopes: 77 additions after deduplicating four proposals into existing GitHub or bedrock.dev scopes. Classify the additions as 51 platform/host scopes and 26 reference/tool scopes.
- Register 367 dated primary-source observations and outcomes. The complete source register now contains 2,145 records; the catalog embeds 1,510 source records. Preserve historical findings and enrich 30 existing services.
- Extend all six game guides (Skyrim SE, Fallout 4, Minecraft, Sims 4, Hytale and Cyberpunk 2077), add an other-games guide, and document actual item/profile/media/file inspections with attribution and access failures retained.
- Add executable offline Discord and Bluesky normalizers, 38 defensive tests, operation-specific evidence, and sanitized replay receipts.
- Add three managed wiki mappings for Bluesky, round-three methods and other games; prepare 15 changed wiki pages for synchronized publication.

## Actual extraction evidence

Nine public Bluesky API captures replay successfully: 67 post representations, two profiles, and four follow rows across two partial public-list pages. The posts exercise images, external embeds, quoted records, record-with-media, video and repost actors. Two avatars, a post image and a video poster were fetched and decoded. An HLS master with two variants was retrieved; video segments and playback were not tested.

Discord covers author/webhook/guild-avatar distinctions, component and attachment media, forwarded snapshots, partial update merging and access-limited content retention. Its validation is synthetic; no live bot grant or authenticated message fixture is claimed.

Independent review found six concrete defects across the normalizers. All six were repaired, with reproductions and final implementation hashes retained in the validation receipt.

## Validation

- 280 local Python tests passed, including 71 extraction tests.
- `python scripts/check_research.py` passed: 2,145 source records, 160 Markdown files, zero stale records.
- All 26 publication files are checked against the frozen manifest and read back from GitHub after publication.
- Normal GitHub CI remains required before merge.

## Boundaries

This expands research and executable normalization, without claiming universal platform completion. Native follows, full authenticated feeds, paid entitlements, expired media refresh and complete downloads retain their separate acceptance gates. Raw captures, credentials and downloaded mods are excluded. GameSync Next is unchanged pending a proven improvement against its actual baseline.

title: Prevent stalled job cancellation from blocking UI
body:
## Summary
- Abort failed job requests and perform stream cancellation as best effort without awaiting an uncooperative cancellation promise.
- Preserve the unconfirmed outcome and no-retry semantics.
- Add regressions for stalled body and reader cancellation, with baseline failure and candidate logs.

## Validation and limits
- Exact-main Node baseline: 284 tests passed after reconstructing the verified fixture inputs.
- Candidate: 286 Node tests passed; focused regressions pass.
- Synthetic/fixture tests only. Real browser acceptance, Rust tests, full repository CI and performance remain unverified. Rust offline run was blocked by missing cached axum.
author: Herbertofury

title: Experiment with bounded archive deadlines
body:
## Isolated experiment
A single request-level abort race bounds caller settlement when fetch or a body read ignores abort. It requests cancellation once, prevents late chunks from continuing, and preserves the previous verified result. This targets the existing draft branch, not main.

## Evidence and limits
16 focused tests and 288 existing Node tests passed locally; five paired tiny-chunk runs and a 500-timeout standard-stream memory probe are retained in the experiment evidence file. An initial full-suite attempt failed because the temporary copy omitted fixtures; that failure is retained. An earlier per-read race was substantially slower and was not promoted. A permanently noncompliant reader can still retain its underlying pending operation.

CI for the first candidate failed because the source change invalidated content-addressed audio assets. Those assets were regenerated and their exact remote blobs verified; the final head c8bd6c2660e8aad7fb543807821b82b2d5ba72cc passed workflow run 41893042474. Real-browser behavior, end-to-end performance, deployed/served assets and full application acceptance remain unverified. Keep this isolated until those checks are complete.
author: Herbertofury

title: Experiment with local gallery snapshot comparison
body:
## Scope
Add an explicit, user-triggered comparison of a locally saved Modrinth project JSON archive against the existing source-owned public Sodium Atlas card. The selected file stays in the browser; the UI fetches the public fixture only from the same origin and sends no comparison request to Modrinth. The existing archive reader and gallery comparator perform the comparison. Matching, changed, unknown and error states are shown; cancellation, stale-response protection and last-successful-result retention are supported.

The card is a saved public Atlas snapshot. A matching set of gallery URL pairs does not prove that images decode, players work, media is current, or the complete gallery is represented. The UI does not autoplay media.

## Verification at current head
Commit `a723e81c73f403190ef44a9f8bea26e0f564f4f1` was built and run locally in Chromium. The actual Atlas app collected a live public Modrinth Sodium response (`AANobbMI`); that saved archive matched all six URL pairs in the existing source-owned card. Browser checks also exercised changed and unknown inputs, malformed-file failure, cancellation, last-good restoration, keyboard submission and same-origin loaded-asset identity. Browser console errors and warnings were empty. Cancellation used a padded local test file and dispatched submit/cancel in the same browser task because the file read can finish before a later click.

Local verification passed: Python 321/321, JavaScript 305/305, Rust 150 tests, Rust formatting, Clippy and build. Hosted CI passed on this exact commit: [PR workflow 42167966528](https://github.com/Herbertofury/Engineering-Atlas/actions/runs/42167966528) and [push workflow 42167961530](https://github.com/Herbertofury/Engineering-Atlas/actions/runs/42167961530), including Windows and Linux Rust checks and research/JavaScript checks.

Raw local browser data, variants, served assets, hashes and test logs remain in the task workspace under `candidate-tests/evidence`; they are not committed to this PR.

## Remaining limitations
This tests URL-pair comparison against one saved public card and one live collected public record. It does not verify image decoding, player readiness, playback, freshness, complete content, or general media/provider coverage. The local Atlas server enforces `img-src 'self'`, so explicit attempts to load the card’s external Modrinth previews are blocked by CSP; this PR does not change that policy. No merge or deployment is included.
author: Herbertofury

title: Recover empty srcset candidates
body:
## Outcome
The offline site extractor no longer loses the entire selected body to an IndexError when a srcset attribute contains empty comma/whitespace segments. A guard skips empty segments before indexing a token.

## Scope
Stacked above draft #11 at `13af2857af303ac54398a88ba965a966331e1e26`. Existing app patches, fixtures, historical receipts, previous branches and main are unchanged. This is a separate draft, not a merge or adapter promotion.

- Preserve surviving URL order and duplicates, complete selected serialization, literal text and surrounding media events.
- Keep existing per-reference URL filtering, whole-attribute data/javascript/blob rejection, protected-body handling and fullSupportAccepted=false.
- Add a specific WHATWG reference and the observed public input through an additive source fragment.
- Preserve nine failed baseline cases, repaired evidence and one replay-harness origin correction.

## Real source and synthetic fault evidence
One fresh public WordPress response returned HTTP 200: 15,465 bytes, one srcset attribute, six candidates, no observed empty candidate. The unchanged actual response retains the same complete-record hash before and after. Six synthetic cases and three explicitly mutated copies of the public body previously failed; all now retain expected text and URLs. The raw response and prose are not committed. Replays make no network requests or media fetches.

## Verification
- 329 Python tests and 320 JavaScript tests passed, no skips.
- Eight new tests include 216 generated blank-segment combinations.
- Source register/internal links, generated Explorer, card/media identities, existing synthetic benchmark fixture and diff checks passed.
- Independent review exactly reproduced both retained receipts and passed eight new plus 71 existing site-extraction tests.

## Important remaining limitation
This is not complete srcset parsing. The underlying comma-splitting projection still mishandles commas inside URLs/query values and does not validate descriptors. Recovery returns results for some inputs that previously crashed, so newly recovered query-bearing inputs still need publication review. Do not treat arbitrary projected URLs as universally redacted or as a download manifest. New evidence publishes hashes/counts, not arbitrary extracted URLs.

No Chromium retry, browser acceptance, Rust change, image decoding/playback, full adapter acceptance or performance claim. The older nine-case historical replay was not rerun or relabeled. Full Linux/Windows CI must be checked on this revision.

[Protocol, source references and retained evidence](https://github.com/Herbertofury/Engineering-Atlas/blob/fix/srcset-empty-candidates-20261107/experiments/srcset-empty-candidates-lab/README.md).

## Published revision verified
[Full validation run](https://github.com/Herbertofury/Engineering-Atlas/actions/runs/42333249872) passed on `05ce06e79bab9ba95b1b3242ffe673d0d6d1a57e`, including general checks and Linux/Windows Rust. All 11 published files were verified byte-for-byte; the published source exactly reproduces the complete 11-case candidate receipt against the unchanged local public response. This remains a draft with the parser/privacy and browser acceptance limits above.
author: Herbertofury

title: Preserve whole srcset URLs
body:
## Outcome
Preserve complete srcset URL tokens before public filtering. Commas inside query values, fragments, paths or rejected userinfo no longer manufacture extra references or expose suffixes as relative paths.

Stacked above draft #12 at `05ce06e79bab9ba95b1b3242ffe673d0d6d1a57e`. This separate draft preserves earlier branches, main, fixtures, failure receipts and adapter gates. It is ready for preservation/reconciliation during the requested Athena migration, not an automatic merge.

## Bounded implementation
- Implement WHATWG URL/descriptor-boundary scanning using ASCII whitespace, trailing comma recovery and non-nested parenthesis state.
- Keep descriptors opaque, preserving the existing URL-only projection contract. This does not claim valid browser candidates, currentSrc/source selection or image loading.
- Apply existing public URL filtering to each whole token; retain conservative whole-attribute unsafe-scheme rejection.
- Preserve selected serialization, literal text, surviving order and duplicates.
- Inspect Python srcset, sindresorhus/srcset and Prettier parse-srcset source, releases and licenses; record why none was adopted. Eleven primary-source rows are additive. No package installed or executed.

## Retained evidence
- Twelve synthetic cases: incorrect projections **10 → 0**, synthetic marker exposure **7 → 0**.
- Twelve new regression tests include 1,000 generated comma-query cases.
- An independently written three-state boundary oracle matches **105,987** generated inputs, with its script, seed, alphabets and hashes retained.
- The unchanged public WordPress capture has an identical complete-record hash before/after and retains all six source references. No fresh fetch is claimed.
- All **24** pinned WPT splitting-loop raw-token cases match; **212 other cases remain unexamined**. WPT scripts and browser behavior were not executed.
- Public evidence contains sanitized hashes/counts and unmistakably synthetic inputs, no raw third-party body or sensitive URL.

## Verification
341 Python tests and 320 JavaScript tests pass locally. Research/source-index, generated Explorer, card/media asset identities, labeled synthetic example and diff checks pass. Independent review reproduced retained baseline/candidate receipts and found no boundary mismatch. All 13 published files were verified byte-for-byte, and the published source exactly reproduces the retained candidate receipt.

## Limits
Raw bodies/tokens remain unfiltered. Genuine URL paths or malformed author text can contain private information: this is not universal secret detection or permission to publish arbitrary content. Descriptor validity, browser selection, playback, full-adapter acceptance and performance remain outside scope. No denied Chromium operation was retried.

[Protocol, sources and retained evidence](https://github.com/Herbertofury/Engineering-Atlas/blob/fix/srcset-tokenization-20261107/experiments/srcset-tokenization-lab/README.md).

## Published revision verified
[Full validation run](https://github.com/Herbertofury/Engineering-Atlas/actions/runs/42334871509) passed on `460965fe992f6f43af87de17331cbb94e2118a79`, including general checks and Linux/Windows Rust. Main and the PR #12 base head were verified unchanged. The local branch is clean. This remains a draft for Athena migration reconciliation, with the limits above.
author: Herbertofury

title: Verify SQLite storage experiment settings
body:
## Scope
Verify the actual SQLite journal mode and synchronous setting before recording measurements. Reject a non-DELETE journal even when FULL synchronous is set; reject non-FULL synchronization. The checks occur before the write timer, and no durability setting or measured workload is relaxed.

## Verification
- 158 Rust tests pass on Linux x86_64, Rust 1.99.1 and bundled SQLite 3.54.1, including two new settings tests.
- Clippy --all-targets -D warnings passes.
- Full generated storage replay completed 42 samples with equal full readbacks and integrity checks. Both variants retain one transaction and FULL synchronization.
- A separate earlier baseline replay also completed 42 equal samples. Runs were sequential on a virtualized filesystem, so their timing differences are not an improvement claim or a controlled paired comparison.

## Limits
No browser/UI, crash, physical power-loss or target-project acceptance. Earlier failed setup (missing relative experiment modules) and raw logs/samples are retained locally. This is a correctness guard on experiment metadata, not evidence of a faster project implementation.
author: Herbertofury
